name: Midface lift
lead: A midface lift is a cosmetic surgical procedure that repositions sagging cheek and lower-eyelid tissue upward, aiming to restore a fuller, younger-looking cheek and reduce the appearance of a hollowed lower lid.[3][7] It is typically described as suited to patients in their 40s without marked jowling, and it can be combined with eyelid surgery.[1]

Techniques have changed over decades, from approaches such as elevating the malar fat pad to high-SMAS facelift designs that extend the dissection to mobilize midface tissue.[3][7][9] Published evidence consists mainly of surgeon case series and technique reviews.
Within looksmaxxing discussions it appears in the context of combined facial-implant and rhinoplasty results shared by patients.[12]
infobox: Hairline and intraoral incisions, SMAS-based, malar fat pad[3][9]

paras: The midface lift evolved from facelift surgery. Reviews describe a history of techniques, including elevation of the malar fat pad with attention to technique and complications.[7][9] The high SMAS facelift places the flap along the superior border of the zygomatic arch and extends dissection medially so that it affects the midface and infraorbital area, which lower flap designs do not.[3]

Complications are mostly described in the context of related eyelid and facelift surgery. A lower-blepharoplasty review addresses lower-lid malposition and the role of lateral canthal support,[1] and a 892-case review examined dry-eye symptoms and chemosis after blepharoplasty, including with midface lift as an accompanying procedure.[4]

Published studies are retrospective or technique reports rather than randomized trials, for example malar fat pad elevation case reviews and a 10-year follow-up of identical twins with differing facelift techniques.[8][9] Registered trials of hyaluronic acid threads and fillers for midface volume or lifting exist but address non-surgical alternatives.[10][11]
A looksmax.org thread presents a patient's combined cheek, chin, jaw implant, rhinoplasty and midface lift result from a surgeon overseas, with community reaction focused on the overall change.[12]

card.summary: Surgery that lifts sagging cheek tissue; established in facial plastic surgery but backed mostly by surgeon case series.
card.aka: Cheek lift; malar fat pad elevation
card.note: Surgical risks include lid malposition and dry eye reported around related procedures.

quick.overview:
A midface lift raises cheek and lower-eyelid tissue to restore volume and reduce hollowing. It is often discussed for people in their 40s and is frequently combined with eyelid surgery.

Evidence comes mainly from surgeon case series and technique reviews.
quick.mechanism: Surgeons elevate and resuspend midface soft tissue, via approaches such as the malar fat pad or high SMAS flap, through incisions near the hairline, eyelid or mouth.
quick.risks: Reported complications in related eyelid and facelift surgery include lid malposition and dry-eye symptoms. It is major surgery performed by trained surgeons.
